question: Is SQLite free to use commercially?

sources.title: About SQLite
sources.text: The code for SQLite is in the public domain and is thus free for use for any purpose, commercial or private.

sources.title: SQLite Copyright
sources.text: All of the code and documentation in SQLite has been dedicated to the public domain by the authors. Anyone is free to copy, modify, publish, use, compile, sell, or distribute the original SQLite code, either in source code form or as a compiled binary, for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial, and by any means.

sources.title: SQLite Copyright
sources.text: Warranty of Title. SQLite is in the public domain and does not require a license. Even so, some organizations want legal proof of their right to use SQLite. Hwaci will sell a Warranty of Title for SQLite.

sources.title: SQLite Frequently Asked Questions
sources.text: (13) Can I use SQLite in my commercial product without paying royalties? Yes. SQLite is in the public domain. No claim of ownership is made to any part of the code. You can do anything you want with it.

sources.title: SQLite Support Options
sources.text: If you would like professional support for SQLite or if you want custom modifications performed by the original author of SQLite, these services are available for a modest fee.

answer: Yes. SQLite is in the public domain, so you can use it in a commercial product without paying royalties or asking permission. The [copyright page][1] covers the dedication, and the [FAQ][2] states the royalty answer directly. If your lawyers want a warranty of title or you want paid help, that is described on the [support options page][3].[1]: https://sqlite.org/copyright.html[2]: https://sqlite.org/faq.html[3]: https://sqlite.org/support.html
